items.title: Carter Benny — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: We had never met, and I got a cable from Leonard, asking me if I would be interested in coming to London [England] to work for the BBC

ctx.x: But the idea of playing a concert, was it something . . . I mean, it’s so long ago, but do you remember saying, “This is different. This is now . . . ”
Well, I don’t remember saying it, but I certainly must have thought it, you know, and that was also something that I think was engineered by Leonard Feather.
Leonard, of course, was very involved in your recordings over there, for Vocalion

items.title: 66095_Benny Carter oral history interview
items.q: I received a letter from Leonard Feather, and wanting to know if I would be interested in coming to London to arrange for the BBC dance orchestra... And I answered to Leonard that I would be interested

ctx.x: That was something that was brought about by Leonard Feather.
Right. Let's hold it. We'll come to that a little bit later.
